payload.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=mechanisms+of+preference+formation+in+human-AI+interaction+and+cognitive+dependence+on+automated+recommendations&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1145/3765766.3765887\", \"title\": [\"Cognitive Bias in AI Recommendations: Understanding and Mitigating Human-AI Decision-Making Errors\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1145/3765766.3765887\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 11, 10]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7008244\", \"title\": [\"Mechanisms of Functional Regulatory Dependence and Decision-Making in Human-AI Interaction: A Theoretical Model of Uncertainty Reduction and Inertial Thinking (URIT)\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Human-AI interaction offers numerous benefits, but it is also worth paying attention to the potential cognitive and emotional risks associated with it. Both social and instrumental form of interactions elicit genuine emotional responses in users. AI systems that support human decision-making contribute to reducing uncertainty and generating positive experiences. Such interactions foster the development of functional regulatory dependence on AI tools and systems. This article integrates theoretical perspectives and empirical findings on human-AI interaction by proposing a feedback loop model. The model highlights intolerance of uncertainty and inertial thinking as key mechanisms determining reliance on AI in decision-making processes and the development of dependence on these systems. The proposed framework provides a theoretical basis for future research on the psychological consequences of AI use.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7008244\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6147327\", \"title\": [\"Trust Amplification Exploits in Human to AI Security Teams Abusing Overconfidence in Automated Recommendations\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Human-AI collaboration has become a central component of modern cybersecurity operations. Security analysts increasingly rely on automated systems for threat detection, risk assessment, and incident response. While this collaboration improves efficiency and scalability, it also introduces new vulnerabilities associated with human trust in machinegenerated recommendations. This paper introduces Trust Amplification Exploits, a novel class of adversarial strategies that manipulate and exploit overconfidence in AI-assisted security workflows. Rather than targeting algorithms directly, these attacks leverage repeated system accuracy, interface design, and organizational dependence to amplify human reliance on automated outputs. Over time, excessive trust reduces critical evaluation and increases susceptibility to subtle manipulation. We analyze the psychological and technical foundations of trust formation in human-AI teams, develop a formal threat model, and present a taxonomy of exploitation mechanisms. Through realistic case studies, we demonstrate how attackers can weaponize automation bias to undermine defensive effectiveness without triggering conventional alerts. Finally, we propose a trust integrity framework aimed at balancing automation benefits with sustained human oversight. Our findings highlight that preserving calibrated trust is essential for the long-term resilience of AI-enabled security systems.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6147327\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.54216/jchci.110205\", \"title\": [\"Explaining AI Decisions to Mitigate Cognitive Biases in Human-AI Collaboration\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.54216/jchci.110205\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "0f8678fe414c635b38bcf0872eb180dc98aad3834ba1a88bbf8e3a86a173e69e", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "emergent_preferences", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1145/3765766.3765887", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7008244", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6147327", "doi:10.54216/jchci.110205"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1145/3765766.3765887", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7008244", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6147327", "https://doi.org/10.54216/jchci.110205"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
